title: RiF: Improving Read Performance of Modern SSDs Using an On-Die Early-Retry Engine
problem: Modern SSDs with high-density 3D NAND flash experience significant bandwidth degradation due to frequent read-retry procedures. The overhead of conventional read-retry operations prevents full utilization of maximum flash channel I/O bandwidth.
motivation: Read-retry procedures waste valuable flash channel bandwidth, substantially limiting overall SSD I/O performance in modern high-density storage systems.
method: RiF proposes an on-die early-retry (ODEAR) engine integrated into the flash chip that proactively determines whether a read-retry will be needed before transferring data to the offchip controller. When ODEAR detects a retry is required, it immediately adjusts the read-reference voltage and re-reads the page on-die, discarding the previously failed read. By performing retry logic and re-reading entirely on the flash chip rather than offchip, RiF eliminates the overhead of transferring uncorrectable data between chip and controller.
key_novelty: Moving read-retry detection and correction to an on-die engine within the flash chip itself, eliminating offchip data transfer overhead for failed reads.
contributions: Introduces RiF scheme with on-die early-retry (ODEAR) engine for proactive determination of reads requiring retry
Designs flash chip architecture that performs critical retry steps on-die without transferring failed data to offchip controller
Achieves 72.1% average effective SSD bandwidth improvement over state-of-the-art read-retry solutions with negligible power and area overhead
primary_theme: On-die read-retry optimization for SSD bandwidth improvement
